## Summary

The thesis started from a regional transport question — how to represent rail in a regional passenger transport model — and developed into a set of essays on **travel mode choice**, combining economic and behavioural theories within the discrete choice framework.

Its contributions, published in the articles listed below, include:

- **Psychological factors in mode choice.** How environmental concern influences mode choice habits, studied with a mediation analysis, and how psychological variables can be measured and integrated in hybrid choice models (ICLV).
- **New specifications of choice models.** A new family of qualitative choice models based on reference models and generalised linear models, compared with standard logit specifications on regional mode choice data.
- **Model comparison.** The consequences of these specifications for prediction and for economic indicators such as willingness to pay.

The thesis was co-supervised with Patrick Bonnel (LET). [Full text on HAL](https://theses.hal.science/tel-01661687)
